top_paper.title: FrontierChallenge: Evaluating Scientific Workflow Completion
top_paper.summary: FrontierChallenge evaluates end-to-end scientific workflows across domains, revealing that frontier models complete only about 20% of tasks despite high partial scores and frequent claims of completion.

papers.title: Real-TurnTurk: A Multimodal Turkish Corpus for Turn-Taking Prediction
papers.summary: A multimodal Turkish dialogue dataset and genetic algorithm-optimized interpretable rules are used to predict turn transitions from visual, acoustic, and linguistic cues.

papers.title: Is Next-Chunk Reasoning RL Really Better than SFT? Revisiting Training Strategies under no-CoT Data
papers.summary: Mixed supervised fine-tuning on combined reasoning corpora outperforms next-chunk reinforcement learning in efficiency and final accuracy across mathematical and out-of-domain tasks.

papers.title: The Handoff Tax: Continuing Non-Native Trajectories in LLM Agents
papers.summary: Coding agents perform long-running tasks spanning dozens of model calls, tool uses, and code edits. As these runs unfold, users face a practical cost-quality trade-off: escalating to a stronger model when a cheaper one struggles, or downshifting once the hard reasoning is complete. Each switch requires the receiver to continue a non-native trajectory produced by another model. We study how this handoff affects quality and cost, and how varying the trajectory information inherited by the receiver changes the outcome. papers.title: Long-Horizon Audio-Visual Generation for Persistent Stories and Interactive Worlds
papers.summary: JoyAI-Echo-1.5 unifies long-form video and interactive world generation through cross-shot memory, geometry-aware camera control, and rollout-aware training to maintain identity and coherence over extended sequences.

papers.title: Video-IFBench: Evaluating Instruction Following of Multimodal LLMs in Video Understanding Scenarios
papers.summary: A new benchmark evaluates how well multimodal language models follow diverse video-based instructions with visual, audio, and structural constraints.

papers.title: FIRM-Video: Check Before You Score for Reliable Text-to-Video Reward Modeling
papers.summary: FIRM-Video uses checklist-driven verification of temporal visual evidence to build reliable reward models for text-to-video evaluation and alignment.

papers.title: Rubrics as Visual-Repair Context for Self-Evolving UI-to-Code Generation
papers.summary: RubSE improves UI-to-code generation stability by using rubric-guided self-evolution to prevent visual repair coupling and trajectory collapse.

papers.title: Stream4D: 4D-Consistency for Streaming Autoregressive Diffusion Video Models
papers.summary: Stream4D improves autoregressive video generation by replacing static 3D critics with a dynamic 4D reconstruction reward and motion prior to preserve coherent motion and reduce geometric drift.

papers.title: VoiceMem: Streaming Dual-Brain Memory for Real-Time Interaction
papers.summary: VoiceMem introduces a dual-brain streaming memory architecture for speech language models that improves retrieval accuracy, emotional personalization, and real-time efficiency.

papers.title: Gated Recurrent Transformers: Expressive Depth through Recurrent Modulation in Transformers
papers.summary: A gated recurrent transformer reuses a shared core across depth with adaptive update gates, achieving comparable or better quality than deeper models with far fewer parameters and lower memory.

papers.title: WarpSAC: Towards the Pinnacle of Scalable Off-policy RL by Rethinking Exploration and Exploitation
papers.summary: Off-policy reinforcement learning stabilizers vary with data availability, motivating regime-aware algorithms that adapt normalization and Q-function clipping to improve efficiency across CPU and GPU-parallel training.

papers.title: MA-VLA: Multi-Arm Vision-Language-Action Model for Collaboration and Compositional Generalization
papers.summary: MA-VLA enables multi-arm collaboration by assigning atomic actions to individual arms and using training-time permutations to generalize to unseen coordination patterns.

papers.title: StreamPI: Streaming Multimodal Temporal Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.summary: StreamPI enhances single-frame vision-language-action models with streaming temporal reasoning via instruction-anchored attention and randomized interval training, improving robot manipulation without extra parameters.

papers.title: Open-MOPD: Diagnosing and Fixing Capability Imbalance in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.summary: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation suffers from token-level budget misallocation across domains, which is addressed by balancing, dynamic allocation, and reward refresh to recover most of the oracle ensemble's capability.

papers.title: V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Visual Rubrics-Based Reinforcement Learning improves vision-language model grounding by scoring answers on visual faithfulness, reasoning consistency, and instruction following using structured partial credit.

papers.title: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
papers.summary: JIT-Agent is a trainable model that synthesizes adaptive agent harnesses for off-the-shelf LLMs, improving performance across diverse models and tasks.

papers.title: VGI-BENCH: Probing Visual Intelligence in Video Generation Models
papers.summary: VGI-bench evaluates visual reasoning in video generation models through 27 tasks, revealing limited reliability and minimal self-correction during generation.

papers.title: Are Android GUI Agents Robust Against Runtime Anomalies? AnTrap: Evaluating Agents in Dynamic Adversarial Environments
papers.summary: AnTrap benchmarks GUI agent robustness by injecting dynamic anomalies into execution trajectories, revealing universal vulnerabilities and distinguishing learnable traps from intrinsic reasoning limits.

papers.title: Super Star: Towards Streaming Real-time Interactive Agents for Digital Humans
papers.summary: A real-time framework for online co-speech gesture generation uses a causal multimodal autoregressive model with streaming speech and motion history, supported by synthetic dialogue data and continual user-feedback adaptation.

papers.title: D^3-MOPD: Adaptive Dynamic Domain ScheDuling for Efficient Multi-Teacher Distillation
papers.summary: D³-MOPD dynamically adjusts domain sampling ratios during multi-teacher distillation by monitoring per-domain reverse-KL trajectories, improving convergence efficiency and closing most of the student-to-teacher performance gap.

papers.title: A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability
papers.summary: A calculus and framework unify revertible effects and reactive coeffects into a context paradigm enabling spatiotemporal composability for dynamic software components.

papers.title: FrontierChallenge: Evaluating Scientific Workflow Completion
papers.summary: FrontierChallenge evaluates end-to-end scientific workflows across domains, revealing that frontier models complete only about 20% of tasks despite high partial scores and frequent claims of completion.

papers.title: Agent-G^2: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Agent-G² models hint depth as a Gaussian distribution estimated online from existing rollouts, improving reinforcement learning on long-horizon tasks without extra probing.

papers.title: Code World Model: Coding Agent as World Brain
papers.summary: Code World Model separates persistent world dynamics from visual rendering by using a language model to generate executable state updates and a video model to render observations from proxy representations.

papers.title: VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning
papers.summary: VBBR-Pro introduces a closed-loop testbed that enables scalable, verifiable, and controllable native visual reasoning through generation across diverse visual substrates.

papers.title: MemUse: Moving Memory Evaluation from Direct QA to Natural Integration in Long-Term Human-AI Conversation
papers.summary: Direct QA benchmarks for conversational memory do not predict user satisfaction, whereas natural integration of prior context does, revealing a large gap between elicited recall and conversational use.

papers.title: MARS: Multi-Specialist LLM Relay System for Competitive Programming
papers.summary: MARS uses retrieval-augmented specialist agents for algorithmic topics to iteratively generate, test, and refine C++ solutions, improving competitive programming pass rates with lower cost.

papers.title: When "Must" Becomes "Maybe": Constraint Weakening in LLM Agent Workflows
papers.summary: Multi-stage LLM workflows lose operational constraints when intermediate artifacts transform binding prerequisites into non-binding context, causing safety failures despite preserved content.

papers.title: Autonomous Mathematical Discovery in an Open-World Multi-Agent Environment
papers.summary: We study autonomous mathematical discovery in the Station, an open-world multi-agent environment in which AI agents from different model families pursue a shared research goal without a central coordinator or scripted pipeline. Agents choose their own research directions, conduct experiments, collaborate, and build a shared scientific literature. papers.title: SecOPD: Mitigating Adaptive Prompt Injections by On-Policy Distillation
papers.summary: SecOPD improves defense against adaptive prompt injection by using token-level feedback during fine-tuning, sharply reducing attack success rates on language models.
